questions.question: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 6%. Stock B represents 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. Stock C represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock D represents the remaining 30% of the portfolio and has a negative return of 5%. What is the average return of the portfolio?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weighted average return = Sum of (Weight × Return) ÷ Total weight

⇒ [(20 × 6) + (30 × 8) + (20 × 4) + (30 × −5)] ÷ 100

⇒ (120 + 240 + 80 − 150) ÷ 100

⇒ 290 ÷ 100 = 2.9%

questions.question: Simplify 13 - [7- (4 + 7) - {7 - (7 - 4 + 7)} + 14]
questions.solution:
Given:

Expression: 13 - [7 - (4 + 7) - {7 - (7 - 4 + 7)} + 14]

Formula used:

Use the BODMAS rule (Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

Calculations:

Step 1: Simplify the innermost brackets.

13 - [7 - (4 + 7) - {7 - (7 - 4 + 7)} + 14]

⇒ 13 - [7 - 11 - {7 - 10} + 14]

Step 2: Simplify the curly brackets.

⇒ 13 - [7 - 11 - {7 - 10} + 14]

⇒ 13 - [7 - 11 +3 + 14]

Step 3: Simplify the square brackets.

⇒ 13 - [7 - 11 + 3 + 14]

⇒ 13 - [13]

Step 4: Perform the subtraction.

⇒ 13 - 13 = 0

∴ The value of the expression is 0.

questions.question: In a clearance sale, a sari whose marked price was ₹10,490 is now sold for ₹9,441. What is the discount percentage on the sari?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

Discount = 10490 − 9441 = 1049

Since 1049 is exactly 1/10th of the Marked Price 10490, the discount is 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = ₹10,490

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = ₹9,441

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Discount = MP − SP

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f66b7b7a21c19b86018182531a3de7bd4d09a8dc62dc26911612a21a0717d097.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 10,490 − 9,441 = 1,049

⇒ Discount % = (1049 ÷ 10490) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given, the net equivalent discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Markup Percentage

Markup is always calculated over the Cost Price (CP). Markup % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: A pipe can fill an overhead tank in 12 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom, it is filled in 18 hours. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by the leak to empty the tank = (T₁ × T₂) ÷ (T₂ − T₁)

Here, T₁ = 12 hours (without leak) and T₂ = 18 hours (with leak).

Required time = (12 × 18) ÷ (18 − 12)

⇒ 216 ÷ 6 = 36 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by the pipe to fill the tank = 12 hours

Time taken to fill the tank with the leak = 18 hours

**Method Used:**

Total Work = LCM of times taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Source**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pipe
 12
 36
 36 ÷ 12 = 3
 
 

 Pipe + Leak
 18
 36 ÷ 18 = 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the leak be L.

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe + Efficiency of Leak = Overall Efficiency

⇒ 3 + L = 2

⇒ L = 2 − 3 = −1 unit/hour

⇒ The negative sign signifies that the leak empties the tank at 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Time taken by the leak to empty the full tank = Total Work ÷ Emptying Efficiency

⇒ Time = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns - Leakage Concept

If a pipe fills a tank in *x* hours and a leak empties it in *y* hours, the net part filled in 1 hour = (1/*x*) − (1/*y*).

Total Work Strategy

The total capacity of the tank is generally assumed to be the LCM of all individual times given. This helps in avoiding complex fractional calculations.

Positive and Negative Work

Filling pipes do positive work and have a positive (+) efficiency. Emptying pipes or leaks do negative work and have a negative (−) efficiency.
</p

questions.question: Two triangles EFG and HIJ are congruent. If the area of ΔEFG is 124 cm², then the area of ΔHIJ will be

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Congruent triangles have exactly the same size, shape, and enclosed area.

If ΔEFG ≅ ΔHIJ, then Area of ΔHIJ = Area of ΔEFG.

Since the Area of ΔEFG is given as 124 cm².

Therefore, the Area of ΔHIJ is also 124 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 124 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔEFG and ΔHIJ are congruent triangles (ΔEFG ≅ ΔHIJ).

Area of ΔEFG = 124 cm²

**Concept Used:**

When two triangles are congruent, their corresponding sides and angles are perfectly equal, which means they cover the exact same region and possess equal area.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of ΔHIJ = Area of ΔEFG

⇒ Area of ΔHIJ = 124 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence vs Similarity

Congruent triangles have exactly the same area. In contrast, similar triangles only have the same shape, and the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Conditions for Congruence

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they satisfy any of the five standard criteria: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), or RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

Area of a Triangle

The general formula for the area of a triangle is Area = 1/2 × base × height. Since congruent triangles possess equal corresponding bases and equal corresponding altitudes, their areas are naturally identical.

questions.question: Let a + b = 2c, then which of the following expressions is true?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let distinct values a = 1 and b = 3. Since a + b = 2c, we get 1 + 3 = 2c ⇒ c = 2.

Substitute a = 1, b = 3, and c = 2 into the given expressions to find the correct one.

Check the expression: a² + 2bc = b² + 2ac

LHS = 1² + 2 × 3 × 2 = 1 + 12 = 13

RHS = 3² + 2 × 1 × 2 = 9 + 4 = 13 (LHS = RHS)

**∴ The correct answer is a² + 2bc = b² + 2ac.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b = 2c

**Formula Used:**

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ a + b = 2c

Multiplying both sides by (a − b), we get:

⇒ (a + b)(a − b) = 2c(a − b)

⇒ a² − b² = 2ac − 2bc

Rearranging the terms from both sides:

⇒ a² + 2bc = b² + 2ac

**∴ The correct answer is a² + 2bc = b² + 2ac.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares Formula

The identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is commonly used to simplify algebraic equations by generating symmetrical terms on both sides of the equation.

Value Substitution Trick

For algebraic equations with unknown variables, substituting simple distinct numbers (like 1, 2, 3) into the options often reveals the correct expression rapidly without complex derivations.

Linear Equations & Averages

The relation a + b = 2c can also be interpreted as c being the arithmetic mean (average) of a and b, which mathematically means c = (a + b) ÷ 2.
</p

questions.question: If the equations 4x + (k - 2)y + 3 = 0 and (k - 2)x + 9y - 5 = 0 (k > 0) are parallel, then find the value of k² + 6.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two lines to be parallel, the ratio of their x and y coefficients must be equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂.

⇒ 4 / (k − 2) = (k − 2) / 9

⇒ (k − 2)² = 36

⇒ k − 2 = 6 (taking positive root since k > 0)

⇒ k = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: 4x + (k − 2)y + 3 = 0

Equation 2: (k − 2)x + 9y − 5 = 0

 
• 
 
•

 y
 
• 
 4x + (k - 2)y + 3 = 0
 
• 
 (k - 2)x + 9y - 5 = 0
 
 Parallel: a1/a2 = b1/b2

**Formula Used:**

For the lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to be parallel, the required algebraic condition is:

⇒ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

**Calculations:**

Substitute the given coefficients into the condition:

⇒ 4 / (k − 2) = (k − 2) / 9

Cross-multiply to solve for k:

⇒ (k − 2) × (k − 2) = 4 × 9

⇒ (k − 2)² = 36

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ k − 2 = ±6

Because it is given that k > 0, we take the positive value for k − 2:

⇒ k − 2 = 6

⇒ k = 8

Now, substitute the value of k into the target expression k² + 6:

⇒ k² + 6 = 8² + 6

⇒ 64 + 6 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Condition for Intersecting Lines

Two lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 intersect at a unique point if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

Condition for Coincident Lines

Two lines are identical (coincident) and have infinitely many solutions if all ratios are equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

Slope of a Line

For a linear equation ax + by + c = 0, the slope (m) is given by −a/b. Parallel lines always possess strictly equal slopes.
</p

questions.question: If x, y and z are positive numbers and x + y + z = 1, then the least value of (1)/(x) + (1)/(y) + (1)/(z) is:
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ For symmetric minimum value problems, the extreme value occurs when all variables are equal. Given x + y + z = 1, we set x = y = z. ⇒ 3x = 1 ⇒ x = 1/3, y = 1/3, z = 1/3. Substitute these values to find the least value: ⇒ 1/x + 1/y + 1/z = 1/(1/3) + 1/(1/3) + 1/(1/3) = 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 **∴ The correct answer is 9.**

questions.question: The mean proportional of 8a² and (18)/(a⁴), where a is a positive number, is _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional between two terms x and y is calculated directly as √(x × y).

Here, the given terms are x = 8a² and y = 18/a⁴.

Mean proportional = √(8a² × 18/a⁴)

Mean proportional = √(144/a²) = 12/a.

**∴ The correct answer is 12/a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (A) = 8a²

Second number (B) = 18/a⁴

**Formula Used:**

If M is the mean proportional between A and B, then M² = A × B ⇒ M = √(A × B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2e426a51b26f9e5c0956bc920b3f7917b765badddd7ba9e5d653242bbd12d26.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ M² = (8a²) × (18/a⁴)

⇒ M² = (8 × 18) × (a² / a⁴)

⇒ M² = 144 / a²

⇒ M = √(144 / a²)

⇒ M = 12/a

⇒ Since a is given as a positive number, its square root yields a perfectly positive 12/a.

**∴ The correct answer is 12/a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two distinct terms A and B is defined as the geometric mean or the square root of their product. Direct Rule: √(A × B).

Third Proportional

If three numbers A, B, and C strictly exist in continued proportion (such that A:B = B:C), then C acts as the third proportional. Formula derived: C = B² / A.

Fourth Proportional

When four independent terms A, B, C, and D conform to a standard ratio format (A:B = C:D), D evaluates to the fourth proportional. Formula applied: D = (B × C) / A.
</p

questions.question: If (sec alpha + tan alpha)/(sec alpha - tan alpha) = (7)/(4), then find the value of cosec α.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the Componendo and Dividendo rule directly to the given ratio.

⇒ sec α / tan α = (7 + 4) / (7 − 4)

⇒ (1 / cos α) / (sin α / cos α) = 11 / 3

⇒ 1 / sin α = 11 / 3

⇒ cosec α = 11 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 11/3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(sec α + tan α) / (sec α − tan α) = 7/4

**Formula Used:**

sec α = 1 / cos α

tan α = sin α / cos α

cosec α = 1 / sin α

**Calculations:**

⇒ (sec α + tan α) / (sec α − tan α) = 7/4

By cross-multiplying the terms:

⇒ 4 × (sec α + tan α) = 7 × (sec α − tan α)

⇒ 4 sec α + 4 tan α = 7 sec α − 7 tan α

Rearranging the terms to group sec α and tan α:

⇒ 4 tan α + 7 tan α = 7 sec α − 4 sec α

⇒ 11 tan α = 3 sec α

Converting sec α and tan α into sin α and cos α:

⇒ 11 × (sin α / cos α) = 3 × (1 / cos α)

⇒ 11 sin α = 3

⇒ sin α = 3 / 11

Since cosec α = 1 / sin α:

⇒ cosec α = 11 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 11/3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a fraction a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is highly useful for simplifying rational algebraic and trigonometric equations quickly.

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

sec α is the reciprocal of cos α (sec α = 1/cos α), and cosec α is the reciprocal of sin α (cosec α = 1/sin α).

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin²α + cos²α = 1, sec²α − tan²α = 1, and cosec²α − cot²α = 1.
</p

questions.question: Ramesh has ₹18,000. He deposited ₹7,000 in a bank at the rate of 5% per annum and ₹6,000 in other bank at the rate of 6% per annum simple interest. If he received ₹1,160 as simple interest at the end of one year, then the rate of interest per annum on rest of the capital is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest from given parts = (5% of 7000) + (6% of 6000) = 350 + 360 = ₹710

Remaining interest for the 3rd part = 1160 − 710 = ₹450

Remaining principal = 18000 − (7000 + 6000) = ₹5000

Required rate = (Remaining interest ÷ Remaining principal) × 100

Required rate = (450 ÷ 5000) × 100 = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Capital = ₹18,000

Capital 1 (P₁) = ₹7,000 at Rate (R₁) = 5% per annum

Capital 2 (P₂) = ₹6,000 at Rate (R₂) = 6% per annum

Total Simple Interest (SI) = ₹1,160 for Time (T) = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Total: ₹18,000

 

 

 

 
 P = ₹7000
 R = 5%
 I = ₹350

 
 P = ₹6000
 R = 6%
 I = ₹360

 
 P = ₹5000
 R = ?
 I = ₹450

 

 

 

 
 Total Interest = ₹1160

**Calculations:**

⇒ Remaining Capital (P₃) = 18000 − (7000 + 6000) = ₹5,000

⇒ Interest on P₁ = (7000 × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹350

⇒ Interest on P₂ = (6000 × 6 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹360

⇒ Let the rate of interest on P₃ be R%

⇒ Interest on P₃ = (5000 × R × 1) ÷ 100 = 50R

⇒ Total Interest = 350 + 360 + 50R

⇒ 1160 = 710 + 50R

⇒ 50R = 1160 − 710

⇒ 50R = 450

⇒ R = 450 ÷ 50 = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the principal amount for the entire period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

It is the interest calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T and CI = A − P.

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, Difference = P × (R/100)². For 3 years, Difference = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

questions.question: If the length, breadth, and height of a cuboid is 8 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm, respectively, then the volume (in cm³) of the cuboid is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a cuboid is calculated directly by multiplying its three dimensions together.

Volume = Length × Breadth × Height

Volume = 8 × 4 × 6

Volume = 192 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 192 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the cuboid (l) = 8 cm

Breadth of the cuboid (b) = 4 cm

Height of the cuboid (h) = 6 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d689b2b0eadcb66a89ed4d1572f5d0bf74f722fe2f38b740bff8812964ae98a8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cuboid = l × b × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = 8 × 4 × 6

⇒ Volume = 32 × 6

⇒ Volume = 192 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 192 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The sum of the area of all 6 rectangular faces is calculated using the formula: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Length of the Longest Diagonal

The maximum length of a rod that can be placed entirely inside a cuboid is determined by its body diagonal: D = √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the 4 standing walls (excluding the top ceiling and bottom floor) is calculated as: LSA = 2h(l + b).

Cube Properties

When the length, breadth, and height are exactly equal (l = b = h = a), the solid becomes a cube. For a cube, Volume = a³ and Total Surface Area = 6a².
</p

questions.question: What is the perimeter (in cm, rounded off to one decimal place) of the sector of a circle with a radius of 10 cm and of angle 30º? (Use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of a sector = Radius × [θ × (π / 180) + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [30 × (3.14 / 180) + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [3.14 / 6 + 2]

⇒ Perimeter = 10 × [0.5233 + 2] = 10 × 2.5233

⇒ Perimeter = 25.233 cm ≈ 25.2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sector (r) = 10 cm

Angle of the sector (θ) = 30°

π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Length of Arc (l) = (θ / 360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of Sector = Length of Arc + 2 × Radius

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5c5e56e034540190815f5f4a22ae0f57049b4aff84bdc485d8eaaba1f612bc6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Length of Arc (l) = (30° / 360°) × 2 × 3.14 × 10

⇒ l = (1 / 12) × 62.8

⇒ l = 5.233 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the sector = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 5.233 + 2 × 10

⇒ Perimeter = 5.233 + 20

⇒ Perimeter = 25.233 cm

⇒ Rounding off to one decimal place, we get 25.2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle is calculated using the formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The length of the curved arc boundary of a sector can be found using: Arc Length = (θ / 360°) × 2πr.

Area of a Segment

The area of a segment is obtained by subtracting the area of the triangle formed by the radii and the chord from the area of the corresponding sector.
</p

questions.question: If 7845K854 is divisible by 11, then what is the value of K?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the divisibility rule of 11, the difference between the sums of alternating digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Sum of odd-placed digits = 7 + 4 + K + 5 = 16 + K

Sum of even-placed digits = 8 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 25

Equating the difference to 0: 25 − (16 + K) = 0 ⇒ 9 − K = 0 ⇒ K = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The number 7845K854 is perfectly divisible by 11.

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits in odd positions and the sum of its digits in even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's find the sum of the digits at the odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, and 7th from left):

⇒ S₁ = 7 + 4 + K + 5 = 16 + K

⇒ Let's find the sum of the digits at the even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th, and 8th from left):

⇒ S₂ = 8 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 25

⇒ Find the difference between the two alternating sums:

⇒ Difference = S₂ − S₁ = 25 − (16 + K) = 9 − K

⇒ For the whole number to be divisible by 11, the difference must be 0, 11, 22, etc.

⇒ Since K is a single-digit positive integer (from 0 to 9), the only possible valid difference is 0:

⇒ 9 − K = 0

⇒ K = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3 & 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 & 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if the last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11 & 13 (Combined Block Trick)

Group the number into blocks of 3 digits moving from right to left. If the alternating difference of these blocks is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, the original number is divisible by the respective divisor.
</p

questions.question: If A is an acute angle, which of the following is equal to (sinA)/(1 + cosA)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put A = 60° in the given expression.

⇒ sin 60° ÷ (1 + cos 60°) = (√3/2) ÷ (1 + 1/2) = (√3/2) ÷ (3/2) = 1/√3

Now, check the given options for A = 60°:

⇒ Option 1: (1 − cos 60°) ÷ sin 60° = (1 − 1/2) ÷ (√3/2) = (1/2) ÷ (√3/2) = 1/√3

Option 1 matches the exact value of the given expression.

**∴ The correct answer is (1 − cos A)/(sin A).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (sin A) / (1 + cos A)

**Formula Used:**

sin² A + cos² A = 1 ⇒ 1 − cos² A = sin² A

**Calculations:**

⇒ Multiply the numerator and denominator by (1 − cos A)

⇒ [sin A × (1 − cos A)] / [(1 + cos A) × (1 − cos A)]

⇒ Using (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² in the denominator:

⇒ [sin A × (1 − cos A)] / (1 − cos² A)

⇒ [sin A × (1 − cos A)] / sin² A

⇒ (1 − cos A) / sin A

**∴ The correct answer is (1 − cos A)/(sin A).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities relating squared trigonometric functions: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Double Angle Formulas

Used to express trigonometric functions of double angles: sin 2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ and cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2 cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin²θ.

Half Angle Formulas

Used to find trigonometric values of half angles: sin(θ/2) = √[(1 − cosθ)/2] and cos(θ/2) = √[(1 + cosθ)/2] for acute angles.
</p

questions.question: In a ΔPQR, the bisectors of∠Q and∠R meet at point O, inside the triangle. If∠QOR = 107º, then the measure of∠P is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct property for internal angle bisectors meeting at the incentre O:

∠QOR = 90º + ∠P / 2

107º = 90º + ∠P / 2

∠P / 2 = 107º − 90º = 17º

∠P = 34º

**∴ The correct answer is 34º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In ΔPQR, the bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet at point O inside the triangle.

∠QOR = 107º

**Formula Used:**

When the internal bisectors of two base angles of a triangle meet at the incentre, the angle formed is equal to 90º + (opposite angle) / 2.

∠QOR = 90º + ∠P / 2

 

 
• 
 
• 
 
 

 107º
 

 P = ?
 P
 Q
 R
 O

**Calculations:**

⇒ 107º = 90º + ∠P / 2

⇒ 107º − 90º = ∠P / 2

⇒ 17º = ∠P / 2

⇒ ∠P = 17º × 2

⇒ ∠P = 34º

**∴ The correct answer is 34º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incentre (Internal Bisectors)

When the internal bisectors of angles B and C of a triangle ABC meet at point I, the angle formed at the incentre is given by: ∠BIC = 90º + ∠A/2.

Excentre (External Bisectors)

When the external bisectors of angles B and C of a triangle ABC meet at point E outside the triangle, the angle formed is: ∠BEC = 90º − ∠A/2.

Circumcentre (Perpendicular Bisectors)

The angle formed at the circumcentre O by the vertices B and C is always double the opposite angle: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Orthocentre (Altitudes)

The angle formed at the orthocentre H and the opposite angle A are supplementary to each other: ∠BHC = 180º − ∠A.
</p

questions.question: If (7sintheta + 4costheta)/(9sintheta - 2costheta) = (5)/(4), then the value of frac{tan²theta + 5}{tan²theta - 5} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the given equation by cosθ to quickly find tanθ:

(7tanθ + 4) / (9tanθ − 2) = 5 / 4

Cross-multiplying gives: 28tanθ + 16 = 45tanθ − 10 ⇒ 17tanθ = 26 ⇒ tanθ = 26/17

Substitute tan²θ = (26/17)² = 676/289 in the required expression:

(676/289 + 5) / (676/289 − 5) = (676 + 1445) / (676 − 1445) = 2121 / −769 = −2121/769

**∴ The correct answer is −2121/769.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(7sinθ + 4cosθ) / (9sinθ − 2cosθ) = 5/4

Dividing numerator and denominator on the LHS by cosθ:

⇒ (7(sinθ/cosθ) + 4(cosθ/cosθ)) / (9(sinθ/cosθ) − 2(cosθ/cosθ)) = 5/4

⇒ (7tanθ + 4) / (9tanθ − 2) = 5/4

Cross-multiplying the equation:

⇒ 4 × (7tanθ + 4) = 5 × (9tanθ − 2)

⇒ 28tanθ + 16 = 45tanθ − 10

⇒ 45tanθ − 28tanθ = 16 + 10

⇒ 17tanθ = 26

⇒ tanθ = 26/17

Now, we need to find the value of (tan²θ + 5) / (tan²θ − 5)

Substitute tanθ = 26/17:

⇒ [(26/17)² + 5] / [(26/17)² − 5]

⇒ (676/289 + 5) / (676/289 − 5)

⇒ [(676 + 5 × 289) / 289] / [(676 − 5 × 289) / 289]

⇒ (676 + 1445) / (676 − 1445)

⇒ 2121 / −769

⇒ −2121/769

**∴ The correct answer is −2121/769.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ and cotθ = cosθ / sinθ

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d). This property often simplifies ratio-based equations.

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: A number is first increased by 12% and then increased by 23%. The number, so obtained, is now decreased by 34%. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (nearest to an integer)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net change for two successive percentage changes is: x + y + (x × y) / 100

First two increases (+12% and +23%): Net = 12 + 23 + (12 × 23) / 100 = 35 + 2.76 = +37.76%

Now, combine the new net (+37.76%) with the final decrease (−34%):

Net Change = 37.76 − 34 − (37.76 × 34) / 100 = 3.76 − 12.8384 = −9.0784%

The negative sign indicates an overall decrease, which is approximately 9%.

**∴ The correct answer is 9% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial increase = 12%, Second increase = 23%, Final decrease = 34%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100) × (1 − r₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4acf4b4ced3db86161ef732db1c9c6493fdb6cc7a90872a0f2fc24383cc25805.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original number be 100.

⇒ Value after 12% increase = 100 × 1.12 = 112

⇒ Value after 23% increase = 112 × 1.23 = 137.76

⇒ Value after 34% decrease = 137.76 × 0.66 = 90.9216

⇒ Net Change = Final Value − Initial Value

⇒ Net Change = 90.9216 − 100 = −9.0784

⇒ A negative value indicates a decrease in the original number.

⇒ Decrease percentage ≈ 9% (nearest to an integer).

**∴ The correct answer is 9% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

When a quantity undergoes two successive changes of a% and b%, the equivalent overall percentage change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%. Use a positive value for an increase and a negative value for a decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

For multiple successive percentage variations, using decimal multipliers is highly efficient. An increase of r% uses a multiplying factor of (1 + r/100), while a decrease of r% uses (1 − r/100). The final value is found by multiplying the initial base value by all successive factors.
</p

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper claims to sell salt at a rate of ₹25/kg. The cost price of the salt is ₹25/kg. Not satisfied with this, he tries to make profit by removing 200 gm from each kg. What is the shopkeeper's gain percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When goods are sold at cost price but false weights are used, the actual price is irrelevant.

Gain % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100

⇒ True Weight = 1000 gm, Error = 200 gm

⇒ False Weight = 1000 gm − 200 gm = 800 gm

⇒ Gain % = (200 ÷ 800) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Claimed Selling Price (SP) of 1 kg (1000 gm) = ₹25

Actual Cost Price (CP) of 1 kg (1000 gm) = ₹25

Quantity removed from each kg = 200 gm

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6d51da6a364d5cd1d43582afb4ea0479292c7d05d104518e631ab1c1ff46a29.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual weight given by shopkeeper = 1000 gm − 200 gm = 800 gm

⇒ Cost of 1000 gm = ₹25

⇒ Actual Cost Price (CP) of 800 gm = (25 ÷ 1000) × 800 = ₹20

⇒ Selling Price (SP) charged to customer for 1 kg = ₹25

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 25 − 20 = ₹5

⇒ Profit % = (5 ÷ 20) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Selling at CP

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, Gain % = (Error ÷ False Weight) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Selling at Profit/Loss

If goods are sold at a profit of P% but weighed incorrectly, actual Gain % = [((100 + P) × True Weight ÷ False Weight) − 100]%.

Successive Cheating

If a dealer cheats by x% while buying and y% while selling, the overall profit % can be calculated successively as x + y + (xy ÷ 100).

questions.question: A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of 600 metres. The thief started running and the policeman chased him. The thief and policeman are running at speeds of 12 km/h and 15 km/h, respectively. Find the time (in minutes) required for the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 15 − 12 = 3 km/h.

Initial Distance = 600 m = 0.6 km.

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.6 ÷ 3 = 0.2 hours.

Time in minutes = 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between Policeman and Thief (D) = 600 m = 0.6 km

Speed of Policeman (Sₚ) = 15 km/h

Speed of Thief (Sₜ) = 12 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/092ea22a3f1907faa90a5b0f256bb4a61651f22bebfa96459a6581118f1be98b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = Sₚ − Sₜ

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 15 km/h − 12 km/h = 3 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.6 km ÷ 3 km/h

⇒ Time = 0.2 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: Find the area (in cm²) of the sector whose perimeter is 64/3 cm and central angle is 60º. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of a sector = r(2 + πθ/180°)

Given Perimeter = 64/3 cm and central angle θ = 60°.

⇒ r(2 + (22/7) × 60/180) = 64/3 ⇒ r(2 + 22/21) = 64/3 ⇒ r(64/21) = 64/3 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr² = (60/360) × 22/7 × 7²

Area = 1/6 × 154 = 77/3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 77/3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the sector = 64/3 cm

Central angle (θ) = 60°

Value of π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Arc length (l) = (θ/360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of sector = 2r + l

Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f236a8966fa88d5c2cca60cffa0b39f7102e2c1868d3046a817846eaa420c94.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Arc length (l) = (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × r

⇒ l = (1/6) × (44/7) × r

⇒ l = 22r/21

⇒ Perimeter = 2r + 22r/21 = (42r + 22r)/21

⇒ Perimeter = 64r/21

Equating the formula with the given value:

⇒ 64r/21 = 64/3

⇒ r/21 = 1/3

⇒ r = 21/3 = 7 cm

Now, substitute the radius to find the area of the sector:

⇒ Area = (60/360) × (22/7) × (7)²

⇒ Area = (1/6) × (22/7) × 49

⇒ Area = (1/6) × 22 × 7

⇒ Area = 154/6

⇒ Area = 77/3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 77/3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc. The formula is A = (θ/360°) × πr² or alternatively A = 1/2 × l × r, where l is the arc length.

Length of an Arc

The continuous portion of the circumference of a circle. The length is determined by the central angle using the formula l = (θ/360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total boundary length of the sector, which is the sum of the two radii and the arc length. Formula: Perimeter = 2r + l.
</p
